taxonomyNote: Source notes molecular evidence hints at overlap with arctic hare but keeps them separate; 'Alaskan hare' spelling used.
fieldMarks: Largest hare in North America, 0.5-0.7 m long, with very large hind feet (nearly 20 cm)
Fairly short ears; tips are black year-round
Summer coat grey-brown with white underside
Winter coat entirely white except black ear tips
behavior: Most active at dusk and dawn
Generally solitary, but 20 or more may gather in the April-May mating season
Relies on camouflage rather than aggression
habitat: Rocky slopes, upland tundra and brushy areas.
range: Northern and western Alaska (also eastern Siberia).

lookalikes.name: Arctic hare
lookalikes.howToTell: Very similar; separated mainly by range (source says they occupy different geographic ranges).
